BadRequest.description: Bad request, or a query parameter that is not allowed

Forbidden.description: Wrong Host (unknown_host), an Origin header (origin_refused), a scope the device lacks (forbidden_scope; see each operation's x-ainkrad-scope), or an operation marked x-ainkrad-destructive without a live step-up elevation (step_up_required)

Unauthorized.description: auth_failed (any signature or device failure, alike whatever the reason), clock_skew (with server_time), or session_expired

ActivityActor.description:
Who did it: a person (`user`, with `user_id`) or the system (an agent's act is the system's,
its id in `details.agent_id`).

ActivityEntry.description: One audit row about an issue.

action.description: The action without the module's prefix: `issue.created`.

next_before.description: Continue with `before=` this for older rows; absent on the last page.

Actor.description: An agent or a person: who owns an issue, wrote a comment, reviews.

appearance.description: How the client draws its figure.

avatar_url.description: Its uploaded image, shown instead of the figure; absent when it has none.

chain_preset_id.description:
The chain preset it uses in place of its own fallbacks (API minor 18); absent when it
has none. (`run_token_cap`, `issue_token_cap` and `queued_wakes` come with the run
engine.)

description.description: What the admin wrote about it.

figure_state.description:
What its figure shows now. Until the run engine is ported it follows the agent's status
and its open questions and approvals only (never `working`, `thinking`, `loading`,
`confused` or `success`).

paused_at.description: When the admin paused it; absent unless it is paused by the admin.

AgentChainBody.description: How an agent gets its chain: a preset, or entries of its own. Exactly one.

entries.description:
Use these fallbacks of its own and no preset (no account pins: pin in a preset); an empty
list clears them.

preset_id.description: Use this preset of the agent's company.

AgentChainOut.description: The agent's effective chain after its own entry.

preset_id.description: The preset the agent has set; absent when it uses its own entries (or the default).

reply.description: Told to the agent; a denial's reason.

AgentProposal.description: An agent the admin proposes; it is hired only once its approval is approved.

description.description: What it is (API minor 17); like the fields below, applied when the hire is approved.

justification.description: Why the company needs it: shown on the hire approval.

org_role.description: Absent: none (`ceo` and `cto` at most once per company).

palette_id.description: One of `listPalettes`; absent: the company's least used.

reports_to.description: An agent of the company it reports to.

runner_tags.description: Capabilities a runner must offer, e.g. `macos`.

team_id.description:
A team of the company to seat it on (with `team_role`, default `member`); a product
owner or lead seat the team has filled is a 409.

AgentSecret.description: A secret for the session: the broker's secret `name`, delivered under `var`.

var.description:
`[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`, not `PATH`, `HOME` or a loader's: the value (`env` delivery), the
path of a 0600 file holding it (`file`), or of an askpass helper (`askpass`).

AgentSession.description: An agent session: a harness on a runner.

harness_session.description: The harness's own session id, what a resume continues.

resumes.description: How many times it was resumed.

secrets.description: The secrets it is leased at each start, by name.

body.description:
A harness event, or the session's own (`started`, `message`, `approval_request`,
`approval_decided`, `interrupted`, `gap`, `ended`), redacted.

seq.description: From 1, by one: replay from any `seq` with `after`.

AgentUpdate.description:
What to change about an agent; absent fields stay, `null` clears `effort`, `sandbox` and
`reports_to`. At least one field is needed.

guidelines.description: At most 50, each 1-500 characters; replaces the list.

reports_to.description: An agent of the company that does not report to this one; `null`: nobody.

runner_tags.description: At most 20 tags, each 1-64 characters without spaces.

AgentUsage.description: Tokens used, as the harness reported them.

cost_usd_micros.description: Millionths of a US dollar, when the harness says.

ApiVersion.description: The contract a server speaks: `/api/<major>` and its additions so far.

minor.description: Bumped on every additive change within the major.

Appearance.description: How the client draws an agent's figure (decision #61).

AppearanceChange.description: A new look: a palette, and a figure version when it changes.

decided_at.description: When it was approved, rejected or expired; absent while pending.

payload.description: What is asked, by kind (the sprint's issues, the command, the overrun, ...).

sas.description: The SAS shown on both screens.

scopes.description: Narrower scopes than the pairing bound; never wider.

Artifact.description: What an agent published, and where it came from.

redactions.description: Secrets redacted from its content before it was stored (text artifacts only).

unscanned.description: Stored as it is, never scanned for secrets (not text: images, PDF, zip).

entity_id.description: A numeric entity id; absent for a device, which is named by `entity_ref` only.

entity_ref.description: The entity's public id: a device's opaque `d_…` id, else `entity_id` as text.

AuditPage.description:
A page of the audit log, newest first. `next_before` continues with older rows, absent on
the last page.

hard_stop.description: Runs stop at the cap (the default), or it only warns.

scope.description: The company itself, or one of its departments, projects, agents, sprints or issues.

token_cap.description: Tokens, 0 or more; 0 with a `usd_cap_micros` is a dollars-only budget.

usd_cap_micros.description:
Millionths of a dollar, 0 or more, enforced beside the tokens when set (API minor 18);
absent clears it. The dollars counted are the priced ones.

BudgetStanding.description: A budget and its spend in the current period.

raised.description: Tokens added for the period by approved overruns.

raised_usd_micros.description: Dollars added for the period by approved overruns, in millionths (API minor 18).

usd_cap_micros.description:
Millionths of a dollar beside the tokens, when set; with `token_cap` 0, dollars only
(API minor 18).

usd_spent_micros.description: Priced dollars spent in the period, in millionths (API minor 18).

left.description: Points left at the end of the day.

scope.description: Points in scope that day (API minor 19); absent on a sprint's burndown.

CfdDay.description: One day of a cumulative flow diagram.

counts.description: Issues in each state at the day's end, every state present (zero when empty).

ChainEntryBody.description: One entry of a chain, tried in order.

account_id.description:
Pin the entry to one account of the company's pool; absent: any. (No account is in a
pool until the accounts slice, so a pin is refused for now.)

ChainPresetBody.description: A preset to store; `PUT` replaces all of it.

entries.description: At most 20; an account pin must be in the company's pool.

is_default.description: Make it the company's default chain (the old default stops being it).
The chain agents with no chain of their own use.

challenge.description:
32 bytes, base64url (43 characters), opaque to the client; spend it once within
`expires_in` seconds.

options.description:
A passkey device's step-up only: `{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions}`
over `challenge`, for `navigator.credentials.get`.

device_id.description: The device that will answer it, `d_…`.

ClaimBody.description:
A claim. The credential hash is SHA-256 of the canonical typed code (upper-cased, dashes
and spaces dropped, `I`/`L` read as `1` and `O` as `0`: 10 ASCII Crockford characters), or
of the QR secret's 16 decoded bytes (not its base64 text). Vectors:
`crates/server/tests/vectors/pairing-v1.json`.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

pop.description:
The routine key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-PAIR-V1` LF `<core_fp>` LF `<base64url of the credential hash>` LF
`<fp(routine)>` LF `<fp(stepup) or ->`, no trailing newline; fp is base64url SHA-256 of
the SPKI.

pop_stepup.description: The step-up key over the same string, with `stepup_spki`.

routine_spki.description: The routine key: a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url.

stepup_spki.description: The step-up key, where the device has one.

core_spki.description: The Core identity SPKI, base64url: its fingerprint must equal the QR's `c`.

device_id.description: The new device, `d_…`, pending until approved.

pairing_id.description:
The pairing, `p_…`: with `core_spki` and its own key the device computes the SAS
itself and shows that, rather than trusting `sas` from whoever answered.

sas.description:
Show this; the approver compares it with theirs. The first 16 upper-case Crockford
characters of SHA-256(`AINKRAD-SAS-V1` ‖ core_spki ‖ routine_spki ‖ pairing id as
UTF-8), as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`.

carry_to.description: A planned sprint to carry the unfinished issues to; else they go back to the backlog.

run_id.description: The run it was written from, for an agent's comment.

account_ids.description: The pool accounts its runs may use (E15.1); empty until the accounts slice.

color.description: Its colour, `#rrggbb`; absent when unset, as every optional field here.

description.description: What it does, for its agents (empty when unset).

logo_url.description: Its uploaded logo (`getCompanyLogo`); absent when it has none.

work_days.description: Working days as a bitmask: bit 0 Monday ... bit 6 Sunday (31 = Monday to Friday).

color.description: The profile fields (API minor 17): absent stays, `null` clears an optional one.

anyOf.description: The admin's own company, or a client's (E15.14).

CompanySkill.description: A skill version of a company (`AgentSkill` in the monolith's contract).

attached_id.description: The department or project id, or the role.

bytes.description: Its body's size; a run gets as many as fit `skills.budget_bytes`, most specific first.

CreateAccount.description:
Request body to create an account. `deny_unknown_fields` refuses any attempt to send a raw
credential value, token, or host file path.

delivery.description: Delivery type (`env`, `file`, `askpass`); read from `core_secrets` when the secret exists.

runners.description: Runner ids allowed to lease the secret; read from `core_secrets` when the secret exists.

secret_name.description: Name of the broker secret in `core_secrets`; defaults to `label`.

Criterion.description: One acceptance criterion of an issue.

raise_tokens.description: Refused here: a raise widens spend and has its own step-up route (`raiseApproval`).

reply.description: Goes back to the agent that asked.

Deleted.description: The answer to a delete: the id that is gone.

head_agent_id.description: The agent that heads it; absent when it has none.

DepartmentUpdate.description: What to change about a department; absent fields stay, `null` clears the head.

anyOf.description: Who may deploy to an environment.

Device.description: A device: who it is and what it may do. Never a key's private half: the Core has none.

fingerprint.description: base64url SHA-256 of its routine public key: what pairing shows.

key_storage.description: Where its key lives, as the device claims it (not verified).

last_used_at.description: Marked at most once a minute.

scopes.description: What it may do (E1-09 enforces them).

stepup.description: Whether it enrolled a step-up key, so it can elevate (E1-09.3).

DodRule.description: One definition-of-done rule and whether it is on (API minor 18).

anyOf.description: How hard an agent thinks (API minor 17).

elevated_until.description: Until when this session may call routes marked `x-ainkrad-destructive`.

url.description: Empty when it has none; never holding credentials.

key.description: `KEY-E3`: its project's key and its number there, never reused.

epic_id.description: Absent takes it out of its epic.

EpicPatchBody.description:
An epic's fields to change (API minor 18); absent fields keep their value, `null` clears an
optional one.

requirement_id.description: One of the project company's requirements.

ErrorBody.description: A JSON error: a stable `code` and a message for people.

error_id.description:
`err_` and a ULID, unique to this answer: logged with it (and, for a refused write,
audited as `api.refused`), for the app's "Copy error".

server_time.description: The server's clock in unix seconds, on a `clock_skew` refusal only (handshake spec §5.3).

points.description: Story points; absent clears the estimate.

Event.description:
One entry of the event stream. `seq` only grows: it is the replay cursor, counted gap-free over
the events this device's scopes may see (`x-event-scopes`), so it differs between devices
with different scopes. New kinds may be added: a client skips an event whose kind it does not
know.

kind.description:
What happened: `audit` (an audited change; the payload is the audit row: `audit_seq`,
`action`, `actor_kind`, `actor_id`, `entity_kind`, `entity_id`, `entity_ref`, `details`;
a device is named by its `d_…` id in `entity_ref`, with `entity_id` null), or a kind a
module writes. The registered kinds are listed in `x-event-kinds`.

EventActor.description: Who acted, on an audited change.

anyOf.description:
What an agent's figure shows, first match wins:

| state | when |
|---|---|
| `sleepy` | the agent is paused |
| `rest` | it waits on its hire approval, or is terminated |
| `listening` | it has an open question to the admin, or an approval it asked for is pending |
| `working` | its run is running and has produced output |
| `thinking` | its run is running, no output yet |
| `loading` | its run is queued or claimed by a runner, not yet started |
| `confused` | its last run failed, timed out, lost its runner or stalled |
| `success` | its last run succeeded in the last five minutes |
| `idle` | otherwise |

Until the run engine is ported only the first three and `idle` occur.

ForgeHosts.description: The hosts allowed besides the public ones.

added.description: Added by an operator, e.g. a self-hosted GitLab.

public.description: Always allowed: GitHub, GitLab.com and Linear.

Handshake.description: What the server is and speaks, for anyone.

api_minor.description: The contract minor this server speaks (`GET /api/v1/me` has it too).

git_sha.description: The commit it was built from (short sha), when the build knew it.

identity_fingerprint.description:
`core_fp`: base64url SHA-256 of the Core identity key's SPKI, 43 characters. Signed
into every request (handshake spec §5.2).

supported_minors.description:
Every minor a client may have been built against and still be served: 0 up to
`api_minor`.

HandshakeBody.description: A liveness proof request: a fresh nonce from the client.

nonce.description: 16 random bytes, base64url without padding (22 characters).

HandshakeProof.description:
`POST /handshake`'s answer: `GET`'s fields plus the proof, which is always present (review
L4). A client that pinned `core_fp` aborts with `core_identity_mismatch` when either is
missing or fails, and never falls back to `GET /handshake` (spec §13).

core_sig.description:
The Core identity key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-CORE-V1` LF `<host>` LF `<nonce>`, no trailing newline; `host` is the Core's
configured Host (the `Host` it requires), `nonce` the text the client sent.

core_spki.description:
The Core identity key, a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url. Its fingerprint is
`identity_fingerprint`.

identity_fingerprint.description: `core_fp`, as in `GET /handshake`; a client checks `fp(core_spki)`, not this claim.

checkout_run_id.description: The run holding the issue, while one does.

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria, in order (API minor 18).

priority.description: Bumped by the admin (`bumpIssue`): its wakes go first.

rank.description: Backlog order within the project: lower first.

repo_implicit.description:
True when the issue has no explicit repo and its project has several, so it works in the
primary one (API minor 20). Set on a single-issue read; omitted when false.

requirement_id.description: The requirement it serves (E15.10), Quest's requirement tag.

age_secs.description: Created → done, or → now while open.

done_at.description: Last done, while it is done.

IssuePatchBody.description: The fields of an issue the admin edits (API minor 18); absent fields keep their value.

repos.description: The repos it touches, in the project's order.

body_truncated.description: The body was cut to 16 KiB in a list.

proposed_by_agent_id.description: The agent that proposed it; absent for an entry the admin added.

rationale.description: The proposer's one-line reason for it.

reason.description: Why it was accepted or rejected.

status.description: `retired`: kept for history, never given to a run.

superseded_by.description: The entry that replaced this one.

target.description: What accepting a proposal applies its body to: `spec` or `profile.<field>`.

updated_at.description: Its last audited change (`created_at` when none).

KnowledgeDecision.description: A human's decision on a proposal.

Label.description: A label of a project, put on its issues.

name.description: One line, 1–50 characters, unique in the project.

LatestEvent.description: The newest event's seq a client would be shown: the catch-up target.

floor.description:
The retention floor: events up to it were trimmed, so a client whose last read seq is
below it re-syncs (E1-04.4). Absent from servers before API minor 2.

LeaseGrant.description:
A granted lease: hand `lease` to the runner, which redeems it once before `expires_at`.
No `Debug` (review L4): a log line must never print a live lease.

lease.description: `l_…`; only its runner can redeem it.

LeasedSecret.description: A redeemed secret, for the runner only. No `Debug`.

expires_at.description: Drop it by then, or at the session's end.

secret_name.description: The broker secret holding the API token, `citadel.linear.<name>`.
The broker secret holding the API token (never the token).

Lockout.description: A key that is locked now.

strikes.description: Locks in a row; each doubles the next.

Me.description: The calling device and what the server speaks.

capacity.description: Points it takes on per sprint; absent when not set.

ModelFallback.description: One entry of the fallback chain, tried in order after the agent's own harness and model.

ModelTier.description:
The (harness, model) an agent's tasks of `tier` start on. Its own harness and model are
its standard tier, so only `small` and `large` are set here.

anchor_issue_id.description: The issue to go before or after.

anyOf.description: Where an issue goes in its project's order.

Named.description: A device: who, by id and name.

NewAgentSession.description: A session to start. No `Debug`: the prompt is the caller's.

secrets.description: At most 16. Each is leased to the runner at each start (secrets broker, gate G-SEC).

workspace.description:
The repo and worktree to work in (`{"repo_url", "base_branch", "branch", …}`); absent, a
scratch dir.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry safe: the same key on the same issue posts (and wakes) once.

wake_agent_id.description:
The agent to wake (one of the issue's company). Absent: the first agent the body
mentions (`@agent:<id>`, or `@<name>`, any case), else the agent working a `todo` or
`in_progress` issue (its owner), else its next actor. An open question on the issue is
answered by the comment and wakes its asker either way.

color.description: The profile fields (API minor 17) are optional; a field out of shape is a 400.

kind.description: `own` (the default) or `client`; anything else is a 400.

assignee_agent_id.description: An agent to hand it to at once, which wakes it.

state.description: `backlog` or `todo`; `backlog` when absent, `todo` with an assignee.

runner.description: The runner's device id, `d_…`; it must be in the secret's scope.

kind.description: `device`, `runner`, or `passkey` (a browser, E1-08; only when the Core has passkeys).

name.description: What to call the new device.

scopes.description: What it may do: within the approver's own scopes; a runner gets exactly `runner`.

apply_from.description:
`now` (the default): from the next cost event on. `past`: also price the metered cost
events of this harness and model that have no dollars yet (API minor 18); refused
until the run engine is ported.

input_usd_per_mtok.description: Dollars per million tokens, 0 or more (as `citadel-server price set`).

key.description:
Issue-number prefix, unique in the company: 1-10 capital letters and digits, starting
with a letter (`CIT` for `CIT-12`).

mode.description: Absent: kanban; anything else than `scrum` or `kanban` is a 400.

sprint_approval.description: Who approves a sprint commit; absent: the owner.

team_id.description: The team that owns it, one of the company's.

team_ids.description: Every team, the owner first (API minor 18); wins over `team_id`.

NewRequest.description: A request to the company, for its CEO to route.

project_id.description: The company's project it is for: a hint, named in the CEO's wake.

runners.description: Runner device ids it may be leased to; default none.

value.description: UTF-8 text, at most `secrets.max_bytes`; written, never read back.

NewSkillVersion.description: A new version of a skill.

attach_role.description: The role (matched exactly against an agent's role).

NextActor.description: Who moves an issue next: an agent, a person, or a timer at `at`.

OrgChart.description: A company's agents (with `reports_to`, the chart's edges) and its departments and teams.

OrgDepartment.description: A department with its teams (the org chart's; `Department` is the flat one).

head_agent_id.description: The agent that heads it; absent when it has none.

OrgTeam.description: A team with its seats (the org chart's; `Team` is the flat one).

Page_Artifact.description: A page of a list. `next_after` is the cursor of the next page, absent on the last.

Page_Event.description: A page of a list. `next_after` is the cursor of the next page, absent on the last.

code.description: The typed code, `ABCDE-FGHJK`: shown once, good once, for 5 minutes.

qr.description: `ainkrad-pair:v1?h=…&p=…&c=<core_fp>&s=<secret>&e=…`, for a QR code: shown once.

PairingView.description: A pairing as the approver sees it.

key_storage.description: Where the claimant says its key lives: a claim, not verified.

sas.description:
The SAS the Core computed from its key and the claimant's: compare it with the new
device's screen, then send it back to approve.

Palette.description: A palette the client colours a figure with.

code.description: The same code as for the options; or `secret`.

credential.description:
The created credential as a WebAuthn `RegisterPublicKeyCredential` (`id`, `rawId`,
`type`, `response.attestationObject`, `response.clientDataJSON`, optional
`response.transports`), binary fields base64url.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

expires_at.description: The pairing's expiry: the credential must be claimed before it.

options.description:
`{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions}` (WebAuthn, binary fields base64url):
ES256 only, attestation `none`, user verification required, a resident key preferred.
Decode it and pass it to `navigator.credentials.create`.

PastRetention.description: The 410 of a replay from below the retention floor (E1-04.4).

floor.description: The newest trimmed seq: every event above it is still there.

PlanBurndownDay.description: Points left at the end of a day, and that day's scope.

PlanDiff.description: The plan now against its approved version: scope added or removed since.

PlanTask.description: A task as a plan version holds it.

Price.description:
A harness and model's price, US dollars per million tokens; each set is a new version, and
earlier spend keeps the version that priced it.

PriceVersion.description: One version of a price, from when it took effect.

anyOf.description: How much an issue matters (API minor 18).

Profile.description: A project's profile. Every field may be empty.

definition_of_done.description: Rules an issue meets before it is done.

definition_of_done_rules.description:
`definition_of_done` with each rule's switch (API minor 18): the rules are the source, and
`definition_of_done` is the text of those that are on. A patch of `definition_of_done`
alone replaces the rules, all on.

network_hosts.description: Hosts runs may reach when `network` is not off (API minor 18).

ProfileActor.description:
Who made a profile change: a person, or the system (an agent's rows are the system's, its
id in `details.agent_id`).

ProfileChange.description: One step of a profile's history.

action.description:
`project.profile_set` (a change), or `knowledge.proposed`, `knowledge.accepted` or
`knowledge.rejected` (an agent's proposal of one).

details.description:
A change: `fields` changed and their new `values` (absent on changes made before values
were recorded), `knowledge_entry` when a proposal made it. A proposal step: its
`profile_field`, `title`, `rationale` or decision `reason`.

seq.description: Its audit sequence number: the cursor of the next page.

ProfilePatch.description:
Fields to change; absent ones stay. The approval policy and permission mode live on
the project and are changed through the same call.

definition_of_done.description: Rules an issue meets before it is done.

definition_of_done_rules.description:
`definition_of_done` with each rule's switch (API minor 18): the rules are the source, and
`definition_of_done` is the text of those that are on. A patch of `definition_of_done`
alone replaces the rules, all on.

network_hosts.description: Hosts runs may reach when `network` is not off (API minor 18).

ProfilePreview.description: What a run on the project is told about it.

budget_bytes.description: The profile's budget (`profile.budget_bytes`); the profile text is fitted to it.

dropped.description: Sections the budget leaves out of the text (named at its end).

text.description:
The project's profile and accepted knowledge exactly as a run's instructions carry them
(a run's skills come first there, and are per agent); empty when it has neither.

ProfileProposal.description: An agent's pending proposal of a new value for one field.

body.description: The new value: JSON, or plain text for a text field.

id.description: The knowledge entry; decided with `decideProfileProposal` (a person only, #48).

rationale.description: Why the agent proposes it, in one line, when it said.

icon.description: A symbol or emoji (API minor 18); absent when unset, as every field below.

runner_tags.description:
Runtime: the tags a runner needs for its runs, the cap on parallel runs, the run timeout
in seconds and how many days worktrees are kept. Stored and shown; not yet applied by
dispatch.

team_ids.description: Every team on it, the owner first; `team_id` is the first.

issues.description: Each done issue, by when it was done.

throughput.description: Top-level issues done in the window.

dropped.description: Sections the budget leaves out of a run's instructions (named there).

injected_bytes.description:
Bytes of the profile a run is given in its instructions, of `budget_bytes` (the
`profile.budget_bytes` setting).

updated_at.description: Absent while the profile was never changed.

icon.description: A symbol or emoji; `null` clears it.

mode.description: Scrum to kanban only with no planned or active sprint.

runner_tags.description: Runtime (API minor 18), stored and shown: the tags a runner needs, replacing the list.

team_id.description: The owning team, one of the company's; `null` clears it, absent keeps it.

team_ids.description: Every team, the owner first (API minor 18); wins over `team_id`.

ProposedAgent.description: A proposed agent and the approval that hires it.

sandbox.description: A development build's token, for the sandbox gateway.

info.description: The Ainkrad Core client API, for the Ainkrad app. Every request is signed by the device's own P-256 key (ES256, raw r||s): the headers Ainkrad-Device, Ainkrad-Session, Ainkrad-Alg (ES256), Ainkrad-Timestamp, Ainkrad-Nonce and Ainkrad-Signature cover an exact canonical string of the Core identity fingerprint, the method, path, query, time, nonce and the body's SHA-256 (handshake spec §5). A session comes from POST /handshake/challenge then POST /handshake/session and lasts 15 minutes; there is no bearer secret, and an Authorization header is refused. A signed body is at most 1 MiB: a larger one is answered 401 auth_failed and counted as a failure against the address, so keep uploads below it. Before trusting a Core, POST /handshake with a fresh nonce and check that core_sig verifies under core_spki and that its fingerprint is the pinned one. Requests carry the server's own Host and no Origin, or the Core's own origin from its web client. A web client signs in with a passkey (POST /handshake/passkey/options, then POST /handshake/passkey/session) and signs every request with a non-extractable WebCrypto P-256 session key in the same way; its event socket takes a one-time ticket (POST /api/v1/ws-ticket) in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol. Times are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds. Versioning: within /api/v1, enum values, union variants, optional fields and operations may be added; a client must keep an unknown enum value (every enum is open) and skip an event or union variant it cannot decode. Anything removed or renamed is a new /api/v2. `info.version` is `1.<minor>.0`; the minor (`GET /api/v1/me`, `versions.api.minor`) is bumped on every addition.

101.description: Switching to a WebSocket. Each text frame is one `Event` (schema `Event`). Closed with 1013 when the client falls behind (a send blocked too long), with the reason `too slow; resume from the last seq read, at most <seq>`: `<seq>` is the last event the server tried to send. The hint is best effort; the client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` set to the last seq it actually read. Also closed with 1001 (no pong), 1011 (server error), 4001 (the device was revoked) and 4003 (its scopes changed: reconnect), with the same hint; with 4410 and `past retention, floor <seq>` when the resume point is below the retention floor (re-sync from `/api/v1/events/latest`)
